question_type: multi-issue row filter + threshold count + geometric mean (three end-of-April MQ-1 Treasury Bills tables, 13-week rows filtered by issue-date window)
decisive_step: Apply the question's February-April window to the 13-WEEK ISSUE-DATE column of each end-of-April MQ-1 'Treasury Bills' table (the May-issue printings: treasury_bulletin_1972_05.txt:4647, 1973_05:4664, 1974_05:4599). The 1974 table opens with a bill issued on the last day of January (line 4601) that must be dropped; then count the Feb-Apr rows strictly above the question's threshold and take every qualifying amount exactly as printed in that pinned release. The reference made the window decision correctly (worklog Step 3: the 1/31 row is marked 'January, excluded'; calc.py comment on bills_1974) but then replaced one printed 1974 cell (treasury_bulletin_1974_05.txt:4603) with the value of the April-1974 printing (worklog Step 5; solution.json decisions), which moved the second output's last decimals and is why the reference was graded wrong. Cells a and c copied the pinned cell literally and were right.

It then listed each year's Feb-Apr 13-week issue dates row by row (a[24]), explicitly excluding the January-issued 1974 row, computed the count and both geometric-mean readings in one calc (a[26]) and chose the qualifying-values reading from the wording (a[27]). One printings call on MQ-1 found no row (a[28]); a answered.

smallest_change.change: show_table (otables.py, the label/type conflict block near line 1220): today a note fires only when a label containing 'date' holds numbers, or a bid/yield/rate/percent/discount label holds dates. Add the mirror case: an amount-like label ('amount', 'outstanding', 'millions', '$', 'total', 'bids accepted') whose column holds `date` values. When that label carries a pandas dedup suffix ('.1') and its base label sits on a num column, print the repaired meaning and borrow the label from a sibling printing of the same table id whose column of the same type is labelled with a date word. For treasury_bulletin_1972_05.txt:4647 the model would have seen under COLUMNS: "- c2,c3 hold dates but are labelled 'Amount outstanding (millions) > 13-week.1' / '> 26-week.1' (duplicates of c0/c1's label): the header lost a group label. Read c2 as the 13-week bill's date and c3 as the 26-week bill's; sibling printings treasury_bulletin_1974_05.txt:4599 and 1973_05:4664 label these columns 'Issue date > 13-week' / 'Issue date > 26-week'; c4 is the maturity date." and the column list itself would read 'c2 Issue date > 13-week [date] (label repaired from 1974_05:4599)'.
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: unlikely: a and c already read c2 as the issue date; the note only confirms it and removes the 'Amount ... [date]' contradiction that a had to reason past (a[14]).

fix.why_not_text: The causal chain began with what the tool printed: b[18] 'Tool mislabels columns ... table only maturity date, not issue date'. Cell a, which had the full advice text, succeeded through its own reading of the [date] tag and column order (a[14]), not through any sentence: nothing in a's AGENTS.md speaks about column semantics, lost header groups or date windows. A sentence cannot restore a header group the corpus lost; the tool can, by reconciling label, value type and sibling printings, and it changes what every cell sees on every table with this defect.
fix.irreducible: No. b's error is fixable at the tool level. The reference's separate failure (a cross-vintage 'repair' of a pinned printed cell, worklog Step 5) shows the opposite risk: v10 text must not tell the model to fix suspected OCR values from other issues; GLM's literal-copy default was right here.

notes: (1) The MQ-1 header is broken differently in each printing: 1972_05 lost the 'Issue date' group (columns carry pandas '.1' dedup labels under 'Amount outstanding'), 1973_05 has the group labels shifted one column right ('Issue date > Unnamed' holds the maturity date, 'Maturity date > Bid' holds the bid), 1974_05 is right. The existing 'header probably shifted' note fired for 1973's 'Maturity date > Bid' (num) but nothing fires for an amount label holding dates, which is the exact gap that misled b. (2) printings cannot follow MQ-1 rows (row label = the amount, rows keyed by date cells), so the vintage rule sends the model into dead ends here (a: 1 call, c: 4 calls, all 'no matching row'). (3) Value vectors hand-typed into calc lose row provenance: c's len() check was the only thing that caught its slip; b printed len() too but had no expectation to compare with; a listed dates by hand. A show_table --where trailer or a calc helper that prints kept rows with their dates and the count would make this check automatic. (4) Gate finding bound b's count literal to a repaired PDO-3 cell b never used (checks/001.json): literal-value binding across tables full of near-identical numbers is unreliable and cost a pointless printings round. (5) show_table regressions worth a test: --long page cut after 9 of 26 rows (a[13]); --from-row 1 skips the first data row (a[16]); '--cols 0-2 --long --from-row 1' printed nothing for 1973_05:4664 and 1974_05:4599 (a[17]); --stitch on a single-part table (b[17]) is harmless but its COLUMNS block is the same mislabelled one. (6) Reference wrong for a different reason (substituted an earlier-vintage value for a pinned printed cell): v10 text should say 'when the question pins a release, use the cell as printed there; report a cross-vintage disagreement as an alternative, never substitute it'.
